conventions.convention: The selected model has G = Z/2, A = {0}, the unique action on A, and zero Postnikov cocycle. Raw vertex gauge labels remain distinct; all higher gauge labels are zero.

For each background, all vertex-spin assignments are allowed, the action is zero, and each assignment has weight 2^(-V_K). Thus the spin partition weight is 1. All fields, measures and amplitudes are dimensionless.
Relative amplitudes fix the background restriction exactly and require identity gauge labels on the boundary subcomplex; boundary spin values remain unfixed and all spins are summed.
Background integration retains component mass |π₂|/|π₁|, which here equals the reciprocal ordinary gauge-automorphism order. The point amplitude 1/2 is an absolute background-gauging amplitude.
Increasing vertex order orients simplices. The interval example uses 0 < 1 < 2, with opposite induced boundary orientations at the shared vertex.
The finite spin model and its boundary prescription are adopted assumptions; deductions establish neither a continuum limit nor empirical behavior.

load_bearing.statement: For the selected G = Z/2, A = {0} finite vertex-spin model, Φ_x = C⁰(K;G), S_x = 0 and μ_x = 2^(-V_K). Background gauge transport is T_g(σ) = σ + g with observable pullback. Relative amplitudes fix only the background restriction, sum all spins, and use the relative higher-gauge sum. Closed physical regulators triangulate closed compact oriented smooth three-manifolds; relative amplitudes are additionally defined on finite ordered subcomplexes.

Adopt as the finite physical model the three-dimensional vertex-spin regulator with G = Z/2, trivial 1-form group A = {0}, zero Postnikov cocycle, zero action, and the normalized uniform measure on spins. The finite background gauging and sewing prescription is part of this adopted model, without a continuum or empirical claim.

For the selected model on a finite ordered oriented complex of dimension at most three in its relative extension, Z_x = 1 and Z_K^(2) = 2^(-V_K)|Ob B(K)|. For a fixed background s on L, Z_(K,L)^(2)(s) = 2^(-(V_K−V_L))|{x : x|_L = s}|. Compatible ordered-subcomplex decompositions with opposite induced seam orientations glue by summing the product of relative amplitudes over seam components with mass |π₂|/|π₁|. The absolute one-vertex amplitude is 1/2. These conclusions concern only the specified finite model.

published_dependencies.used_for: Transitive mathematical supplier defining finite groupoids, reciprocal-automorphism integration and homotopy-fiber pushforward. Read its definition and well-definedness proof.

Supplier of the ordinary gauging theorem on the mathematical seam page; defines compatible triples and morphisms and proves finiteness. The assigned physical theorem instead directly uses the separate higher-gauging theorem.

concerns.concern: The Definition introduces the spin product for 'a closed one-dimensional subcomplex γ', and proof step 2.1 concludes that it is 'a well-defined genuine line observable under [F2]'. The cited def-aqft-two-group-symmetry-realization requires a genuine line to be supported on a closed embedded one-dimensional submanifold. A closed finite graph subcomplex can have a valence-four vertex, for example two polygonal circles meeting at one vertex, and is then not a one-manifold. The spin function remains well-defined, but its asserted classification does not follow for the stated domain. Require γ to represent a smooth embedded closed one-manifold, or distinguish general graph-supported observables.

seams_checked.note: Compared the model-data interface and conditional coupling theorem with their physical consumer. The consumer supplies finite configurations, complete identity-network correlators, coherent translations and phase 1, and explicitly adds its relative boundary convention rather than attributing it to the closed-manifold supplier. The genuine-line domain mismatch is recorded separately against the owned definition.

Compared the mathematical definitions and gauging theorems with the physical statements and proof facts. The physical consumer preserves raw gauge multiplicities, specializes A to the trivial group, and satisfies invariant scalar-weight and factorization hypotheses with W = 1. Absolute normalization, exact relative restriction and seam mass specialize correctly. Both example counts agree with these formulas.
